intent:
"yes approbe and begin the implementation" started the bstack build slice by slice, strictly one at a time ("keep it sequential"). Later: "i'm only not concerned about security hardening, threat-model concerns. Style and simplification and following proper design principles are still important." - build the full app fast, but review the core properly so slices and phases do not leave bugs. Tiny adjacent slices are merged; this piece merges C11b and C11c.

The plans of record are in the repo: `docs/design.md` (requirements and decisions, including R24: licensing is out of scope) and `docs/implementation-plan.md` (tasks, task evidence contract). knowttl/bstack is public, has no GitHub Actions or workflows and no release automation, and ships through the no-mistakes pipeline with automatic merge of green work. Landed: Phase 0, Phase 1 and T2.1 (https://github.com/knowttl/bstack/pull/21: research briefs, `cite-check`, and the completed Phase 1 live vision review).

This piece is merged slice C11bc: task T2.2 "Build `inspect`" and task T2.3 "Build `inventory`". Done evidence: read-only fingerprint and exact missing-prerequisite result; equivalent standards and scoped instruction candidates, absent documents tolerated.

cases.procedure: inspect fingerprints a dirty fixture unchanged including Git index bytes; inspect reports no commits and literal staged rename and untracked paths.

inspect with git hidden from PATH is blocked with the exact named limitation; inspect reads nested manifests and reports missing detected prerequisites; inspect blocks unreadable commit history rather than claiming no commits; inspect reports malformed manifests as a named limitation. Windows npm selection uses Node and a JavaScript CLI with literal arguments; Windows npm resolves a PATH launcher to an executable JavaScript CLI; Windows npm.cmd resolves a PATH launcher to an executable JavaScript CLI; Windows pnpm resolves a PATH launcher to an executable JavaScript CLI; Windows pnpm.cmd resolves a PATH launcher to an executable JavaScript CLI; Windows yarn resolves a PATH launcher to an executable JavaScript CLI; Windows yarn.cmd resolves a PATH launcher to an executable JavaScript CLI; Windows npm.cmd without a supported CLI is blocked; Windows pnpm without a supported CLI is blocked; Windows pnpm.cmd without a supported CLI is blocked; Windows yarn without a supported CLI is blocked; Windows yarn.cmd without a supported CLI is blocked.

limitations: Recorded local runs establish Linux and Node 24 only, not Windows or macOS.
Evidence covers this task slice, not complete audit execution, native project checks, protected edits or the later release acceptance run.
Discovery uses documented name families and regular-file traversal exclusions. Sources need content review to establish authority.

Prerequisite probes report versions for recognised manifests, without asserting all project-specific prerequisites or supported version ranges. Available local history is read without fetching shallow ancestors.

Captain checklist: real Windows execution of npm, pnpm and Yarn launchers remains unverified. Injected win32 tests on Linux cover PATH entry-point resolution and literal JavaScript CLI arguments, not Windows process execution.
